title: deinterleave-heartbeats-from-data-chunks-openai-compat
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Under high-concurrency conditions the OpenAI-compat SSE adapter was interleaving keepalive/heartbeat events with data frames which caused partial JSON objects and tool/function-call sentinel tokens to be emitted across chunk boundaries. This manifested as downstream JSON parse errors and occasional misrouted function call events. This PR separates control/heartbeat traffic from data frames at the framing layer, introduces a small control marker to avoid accidental coalescing with data, and updates the reassembly logic to preserve token/event ordering while remaining backward-compatible with clients that ignore unknown markers. Summary of changes: 1) introduce a dedicated 1-byte control marker (0x1E) and explicit control-frame type in the SSE framing code; 2) adapt sse_parser to buffer and re-emit data frames without interleaving control frames; 3) add per-connection sequence tags to detect out-of-order control bursts and drop stale heartbeats; 4) adjust keepalive/backoff strategy to reduce coalescing windows; 5) update python and typescript openai-compat clients to recognize and ignore the new control marker; 6) add property-based fuzz tests and integration canary harness; 7) add observability: metric redwood.sse.control_frames and traces for control->data reassembly latency. Compatibility and rollout: the marker is ignored by older clients (they see a harmless unknown byte), and the server will continue serving both pre-change and post-change framed streams. Feature-flagged rollout: 5% canary for 24h -> 25% -> 100%; rollback guard included. Linear and support links: ENG-4832, SUP-1247. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration canary, [x] docs snippet, [x] telemetry added, [x] staged rollout plan.
commits: add: introduce control marker 0x1E and control-frame type for SSE framing
fix: sse_parser deinterleave logic and sequence-tag handling
feat(tests): property-based fuzz harness for SSE reassembly and added regression case
chore(clients): TS/Python clients ignore control marker and add tests
diff_snippets: + const CONTROL_MARKER = 0x1E // reserved control prefix for heartbeat/control frames
- // previous behaviour: emit heartbeats inline with data frames (caused interleaving)
+ func (f *Framer) writeFrame(w io.Writer, t FrameType, payload []byte) { /* ensure control frames are emitted on separate frame types */ }
+ // parser: detect control marker and route to control channel handler before data reassembly
review_comments: Kenji Sato: Can you add a regression test that reproduces the parse-error seen in SUP-1247? The fuzz harness is great but we need a deterministic repro for the bug ticket.
Ava Martinez: Added a deterministic integration case under integration/canary that replays the SUP-1247 capture and asserts stable JSON reassembly.
Priya Raman: Suggests lowering keepalive frequency for the first 30s after connection start to avoid immediate coalescing. Updated logic and added telemetry to validate impact.
Liam O'Connor: Approved after one nit on variable naming in parser.go; requested changelog entry. Nit fixed and changelog added.
release_notes: Fixes SSE framing bug where heartbeats could fragment JSON/tool-call tokens by deinterleaving control frames and preserving token boundaries. Adds a backward-compatible control marker and improves reassembly resiliency. Rolled out behind a feature flag; users should see fewer streaming parse errors in OpenAI-compat mode.
